Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: Ethiopia's cross-border payments are partially functional. Inbound remittances via MTOs (Western Union, MoneyGram, WorldRemit, Ria Financial, etc.) are established and functional, with 8 MTOs operating. M-Pesa extended its M-Pesa Global service to Ethiopia in October 2024 enabling Kenya-Ethiopia transfers. Telebirr offers international remittance receipt. EthSwitch (via Ethiopay/Mastercard partnership Nov 2025) enables international card acceptance. However: (1) Outbound retail cross-border payments remain restricted - the NDPS 2026-2030 only 'plans to enable low-value outbound cross-border transfers'; (2) Ethiopia is NOT yet a PAPSS member (Wikipedia PAPSS list as of Nov 2025 does not include Ethiopia, though EthSwitch is in talks with PAPSS); (3) EthSwitch partnered with UAE Central Bank's Aani platform (2025) for cross-border capability. Cross-border is partially functional - inbound works well, outbound is restricted/emerging.
redteam_note: Comment wording may not match the score — re-read (needs judgement).
revision_notes: Confirmed but flagged for human review. As of the newest evidence, PAPSS lists Ethiopia only under its 'Extended Network' for inbound-only reachability (PAPSS Network Coverage report, June 2026) — Ethiopia is not a full/direct PAPSS participant. Ethiopia's National Digital Payments Strategy 2026-2030 and EthioPay IPS launched 9 December 2025 and 'aims to enable' low-value outbound cross-border transfers (ENA, 9 Dec 2025) — still a stated ambition rather than a confirmed live service. EthSwitch's Mastercard partnership (Nov 2025) does provide real operational international card acceptance/issuance. This mix of live (inbound, card network) and aspirational (outbound via the IPS itself) functionality is consistent with 'Partially functional' but the underlying comment blends MTO/card-network channels with the core instant payment system the variable asks about; recommend human review to confirm the code reflects the IPS specifically rather than adjacent remittance channels.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports direct person-to-person transfer of funds between individuals for informal transactions, remittances, and interpersonal value transfers.
Comments: P2P via Telebirr, M-Pesa, EthQR fully operational.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. AfricaNenda's SIIPS 2025 case study documents that EthSwitch enabled interbank P2P transfers using its card-switch infrastructure from 2021, and its instant payment system (live Feb 2024) extends this. M-Pesa's integration with EthSwitch (completed Oct 2025) further enables P2P transfers across 15 banks and mobile wallets. Binary scale (No/Yes) supports code 2 'Yes'.

Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: NBE direct ownership and board control of EthSwitch as national switch.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Revised from 5 to 4. NBE holds a 46% ownership stake in EthSwitch S.C. and chairs its 12-member board of bank CEOs via its Vice Governor (TechCabal, 11 Mar 2021; AfricaNenda SIIPS 2025 case study; EthSwitch board announcement, 19 Sept 2024). However EthSwitch S.C. is an independently incorporated share company jointly owned by banks, MFIs and PSOs — NBE does not itself operate the switch. This is 'Board Representation' (4), not 'Direct Operation' (5); the original single source did not actually establish direct operation.

Definition: Whether payment system governance explicitly includes mechanisms to ensure inclusivity and represent interests of vulnerable populations, including provisions for input from all participant types, consumer representatives, small providers, or explicit financial inclusion mandates in governance documents.
Comments: NDPS 2026-2030 pro-poor focus on underserved/rural inclusion.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Ethiopia's National Digital Payments Strategy 2026-2030, launched 9 December 2025, sets explicit quantitative inclusion targets — reducing the rural-urban digital payment usage gap to ≤8 percentage points and the gender gap to under 3pp, and expanding access for informal traders, smallholder farmers, SMEs, women and youth (BirrMetrics, 9 Dec 2025; ENA, 9 Dec 2025). This corroborates code 3 'Yes'.

Comments: Partial scheme rules in leaked Scribd docs; not fully public.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Revised from 2 to 3. EthSwitch's System Rules and card-scheme documents (ETHQR guideline, Ethiopay card scheme draft/specification, certified vendor list) are published directly and freely on ethswitch.com, and NBE publishes its Person-to-Merchant Scheme Rulebook for the Instant Payment System directly on nbe.gov.et (v1.0, Dec 2023) — all downloadable without registration. AfricaNenda's SIIPS 2025 case study confirms further IPS rulebooks exist. This meets 'Yes - Fully Public' rather than 'Partial - On Request'; the original single source (a third-party Scribd upload of an unrelated GSMA report) did not actually support the original score.
